items.title: Domain Created
items.description: Triggers when a domain is created

fields.name: id
fields.description: unique reserved domain resource identifier

fields.name: uri
fields.description: URI of the reserved domain API resource

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: timestamp when the reserved domain was created, RFC 3339 format

fields.name: description
fields.description: human-readable description of what this reserved domain will be used for

fields.name: metadata
fields.description: arbitrary user-defined machine-readable data of this reserved domain. Optional, max 4096 bytes.

fields.name: domain
fields.description: hostname of the reserved domain

fields.name: region
fields.description: deprecated: With the launch of the ngrok Global Network domains traffic is now handled globally. This field applied only to endpoints. Note that agents may still connect to specific regions. Optional, null by default. (`au`, `eu`, `ap`, `us`, `jp`, `in`, `sa`)

fields.name: cname_target
fields.description: DNS CNAME target for a custom hostname, or null if the reserved domain is a subdomain of an ngrok owned domain (for example, *.ngrok.app)

fields.name: certificate.id
fields.description: a resource identifier

fields.name: certificate.uri
fields.description: a uri for locating a resource

fields.name: certificate_management_policy.authority
fields.description: certificate authority to request certificates from. The only supported value is letsencrypt.

fields.name: certificate_management_policy.private_key_type
fields.description: type of private key to use when requesting certificates. Defaults to ecdsa, can be either rsa or ecdsa.

fields.name: certificate_management_status.renews_at
fields.description: timestamp when the next renewal will be requested, RFC 3339 format

fields.name: certificate_management_status.provisioning_job.error_code
fields.description: if present, an error code indicating why provisioning is failing. It may be either a temporary condition (INTERNAL_ERROR), or a permanent one the user must correct (DNS_ERROR).

fields.name: certificate_management_status.provisioning_job.msg
fields.description: a message describing the current status or error

fields.name: certificate_management_status.provisioning_job.started_at
fields.description: timestamp when the provisioning job started, RFC 3339 format

fields.name: certificate_management_status.provisioning_job.retries_at
fields.description: timestamp when the provisioning job will be retried

fields.name: acme_challenge_cname_target
fields.description: DNS CNAME target for the host _acme-challenge.example.com, where example.com is your reserved domain name. This is required to issue certificates for wildcard, non-ngrok reserved domains. Must be null for non-wildcard domains and ngrok subdomains.

fields.name: resolves_to.value
fields.description: accepts an ngrok point-of-presence shortcode, or "global"

For example, to allow the token to open a tunnel on example.ngrok.io your ACL would include the rule `bind:example.ngrok.io`. Bind rules for domains may specify a leading wildcard to match multiple domains with a common suffix. For example, you may specify a rule of `bind:*.example.com` which will allow `x.example.com`, `y.example.com`, `*.example.com`, etc. Bind rules for labels may specify a wildcard key and/or value to match multiple labels.
